ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: It is known that in triangle $\triangle A B C$, $A=30^{\circ}, C=105^{\circ}, b=4$, then $a=(\quad)$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The problem gives that in triangle ABC, A=30°, C=105°, b=4. According to the sum of interior angles of a triangle, B=180°-30°-105°=45°. In standard notation, a corresponds to angle A, and b corresponds to angle B. By the sine theorem a/sin A = b/sin B, we can obtain a = b·sin A / sin B = 4·sin30°/sin45° = 4·(1/2)/(√2/2) = 2√2. Therefore a=2√2.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/right-triangle construction. Read A=30°, C=105°, b=CA=4, so B=45°. Place A at the origin and AB on the positive x-axis. Since CA=4 makes a 30° angle with AB, point C has height 4sin30°=2 above AB and horizontal projection 4cos30°=2√3. Because angle B=45°, the segment BC meets AB at a 45° angle, so the horizontal distance from C down to B equals the vertical height 2. Thus BC is the hypotenuse of an isosceles right triangle with legs 2 and 2, giving a=BC=√(2²+2²)=2√2.
